thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: High error rate on serving-cluster-us-west-2 (gpu-pool-7). 5xx rate > 15% over 2m. Sample error: 'CUDA illegal memory access' on container model-server-rlhf-3.

dmitri (eng-runtime): seeing repeated stack traces on the node: \n```\nE CUDA: illegal memory access
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error'
  what():  misaligned address when reading KV cache
  at serving/kv_cache.cpp:412
```
node kernel logs show multiple OOM-like hits right before crash.

anika (eng-ml): this started right after the rolling model push of rlHF-v3.1-quantized at ~14:18 UTC? could be reload path hitting a kernel path.

sara (oncall): 14:18 UTC matches deploy-bot message below. I'm going to cordon the affected node and scale up routing to fallback models.

```

sara (oncall): mitigation plan: 1) route traffic for rlhf routes to rlHF-v3.0 (older variant) 2) drain + reprovision affected nodes 3) disable quantized kernel path on runtime if possible 4) notify customers of degraded performance if rollout rollback takes > 30m.

sara (oncall): doing the route change now: \n```\nredwoodctl traffic-shift --from rlHF-v3.1-quantized --to rlHF-v3.0 --percent 100 --region us-west-2
```

sara (oncall): can we get a temporary autoscaling burst so customer-facing traffic doesn't queue?

dmitri (eng-runtime): confirmed: after disabling quant kernel path, canary pod stays up, no illegal access logs. pushing hotfix branch: gh/eng-runtime#849.
